THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a2 lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U9b1a — Lift the MCP compile fence where the namespace path is proved

Operator ruling 2026-10-30 on U9b1's fifth run (in chat, "ok, keep going", then "A", on the controller's recommendation; run 0065-slice-two-unit-u9b1-see-the-d09b2390 stopped IMPL-BLOCKED after its second visit reported oversized): U9b1 lands as two pull requests. U9b1a lands the fifth run's tree. `McpFence::current()` is chosen by host, with no knob: Lifted on Linux, Standing on macOS (ruling 1). It carries rulings 4, 5, 14 and 21, ruling (2) of 2026-10-28, U5a2's F1 and U7d3's L2 and L3. It migrates the suites' fixtures past the lift with no fixture boxed: a seat with no model surface uses the exec driver, and a scripted driver is hired as an office over an operator adapter with synthetic plumbing facts.

U9b1a proves ruling 21's first and fourth cases: a public run with nothing at stake admits its unboxed writers and completes, and a seat without hands holding a provider-native grant retains nothing. Ruling 21's third case is proved by MB2's compile refusal, "MCP capability '<capability>' requires workspace hands at this site". That refusal is earlier than CR2's and stands as the case's proof. By MB2 it refuses a wanted grant too, rather than dropping it. U9b1a closes no task: 42.2, 46.1 and 46.2 stay unticked.

Until U9b1b lands, no release is cut from main, no host engine the house pipeline runs is upgraded past U9b1a, and no realm the house pipeline runs grants an MCP capability.

Controller ruling 2026-10-30 on U9b1a's first run (under the operator's standing ruling of 2026-10-28, on the chief's H1; run 0065-slice-two-unit-u9b1a-see-th-2abb1e94 stopped REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD): while any reservation serves, a writer whose writable reach covers the capability coordination root is refused with MB3's identity cause, in both arrival orders, whatever evidence is at stake.

Operator ruling 2026-10-30 on U9b1a's second run (in chat, "a", on the controller's recommendation; run 0065-slice-two-unit-u9b1a-see-th-49b8e92e stopped REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD on the chief's H2): the coordination records a broker's source lease lives in are protected from every writer Brokkr boxes, on every run. A reservation is a plain file, so a boxed writer admitted while nothing was served could rewrite its own record before a broker extended beside it. A boxed writer whose writable reach covers the capability coordination root is therefore refused at admission with MB3's identity cause, whether or not evidence is at stake and whether or not any reservation serves. No admitted boxed writer can rewrite a reservation, its own included. This narrows ruling 21 for boxed writers only. A writer Brokkr cannot box is still admitted on a run with nothing at stake, and still refuses beside a live broker; it already holds the user's own write, so a forged record gives it nothing more, and refusing it on every run stays the later decision ruling 21 names. No shipped adapter, office, recipe or scaffold binds that root.

Controller ruling 2026-10-30 on U9b1a's third run (under the operator's standing ruling of 2026-10-28, on the chief's H3; run 0065-slice-two-unit-u9b1a-see-th-d93f79f1 stopped REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD): the operator's every-run refusal above holds where the coordination root cannot be opened too. Before an attempt proceeds holding no lease (C1), each of its boxed writers is compared with the coordination root's spelled path by the same test (at, above or below, by path, by identity where anything on that path stands, and on Linux by the mount table), and is refused with MB3's identity cause where it reaches the root or where its reach cannot be proved. A boxed writer kept apart from the root, and a writer Brokkr cannot box, still proceed holding no lease, as ruling 21 says.

Files: the row's files, the existing private children of `engine/broker.rs` its rulings touch (admission, exclusion, observation, settlement, sources), and `crates/brokkr-cli/src/init/adapters.rs` by ruling 5. Owning tests: as U9b1.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR U9b1a, RUN 4 (the controller, 2026-10-30)

Your tree is already the unit's work, staged and uncommitted:
- It is U9b1a run 3's signed commit e8eefdd01 (branch s2/U9b1a-run3), replayed onto main at 1d8955b82, the base run 3 was cut from.
- design.md's U9b1a section also carries a new ruling: the controller's on run 3 (H3), after the operator's on run 2 (H2). Read both first.
- Run 3's commit message is in .forge/u9b1a/commit-msg.txt. The seat results of runs 1-3 are in .forge/u9b1a/run1/, run2/ and run3/; run 3's chief is 6e0076c5-…-chief.json, its positions beside it.

Run 3 stopped on the chief's security hold H3. Run 3's H2 fix (sources::records_kept, called from exclusion::compared before the unstaked return) was confirmed sound wherever admission holds an opened root, and it stays. So does run 2's H1 check in kept.

H3, as the chief found it:
- Where Root::of gives None (any step of the HOME-to-root walk is not protected, e.g. a 0775 HOME under umask 002, or a pre-existing root directory at 0755), admission::coordinated returns Ok(None) for a claim protecting nothing, and admit_in takes unreserved() (admission.rs ~:403-405 and ~:565-569). compared and records_kept never run.
- A boxed writer whose bind covers the root is then admitted holding no lease and leaving no record. From inside its box it can repair the walk's permissions (chmod); hands/sealed.rs seals path, device and inode, not mode.
- A later run's broker then opens the root, finds no record of that writer, and is admitted. The writer can rewrite the broker's serves to [], defeating source exclusion while the broker lives.
- The operator's ruling already requires this refusal on every run; the chief found no specification defect.

This visit's job, in order:
1. FIX H3 as ruled (design.md's controller ruling on the third run; the chief's recommended fix).
   - Before an attempt proceeds holding no lease (coordinated's None arm, or admit_in before unreserved), compare each boxed writer of the claim with the coordination root's spelled path, root::coordination(home), by the same test records_kept uses: covers at, above or below, by path, by identity where anything on that path stands, and on Linux by the mount table.
   - Refuse with MB3's identity cause naming the root where a boxed writer reaches it, and fail closed (Unmounted) where its reach cannot be proved, as records_kept already does.
   - Share one check between the opened-root and no-root paths rather than copying it: for example, make records_kept take the root's path and a mount-table reader instead of an opened Root. Neither staked nor compared changes for anything else.
   - A boxed writer kept apart from the root still proceeds holding no lease. A writer Brokkr cannot box is unchanged (ruling 21).
   - Files: admission.rs, exclusion.rs and/or sources.rs (the row's broker children), root.rs only if the reader needs it, and their in-crate tests.
2. Bind it (decision 0071 ruling 9: exact outcomes and a compiling removal mutation):
   - A root that cannot be opened (make the walk unprotected the way the existing tests do; see the 0775 tempdir cases), with a boxed writer whose rw bind covers the root (at, and above): refused with the exact cause, and nothing sealed.
   - Controls on that same unopened root: a boxed writer kept apart from the root, and an unboxed writer, each proceed holding no lease.
   - The transition the chief names: unopened root → the root-reaching boxed writer is refused → the walk's permissions are repaired → a later broker opens the root and is admitted, with no unrecorded root-reaching writer live beside it. Assert each step's exact outcome.
   - Record the mutation removing the new no-root check failing the new tests, then restore it.
3. Fix the reviewers' wording and evidence findings:
   - Correctness L1 and security LOW 2: the commit message, exclusion.rs's module comment, sources.rs's records_kept comment and evidence/U9b1a.md must state exactly what the code now does, opened root and no root both. Do not write a claim the code does not meet.
   - admission.rs's unreserved() doc comment (~:434-442) calls the absence of a reservation evidence "read under the lock by every later admission". Make it true: that absence cannot tell a later broker a writer is live.
   - Correctness L2: evidence/U9b1a.md must not count writer_lease's seat pass as a real-box proof. In a seat that cannot nest bubblewrap it skips ("skipped: writer_lease: no bubblewrap namespace here"). Say which run executed refused_at_the_door, or that none did in the seat and that the Linux CI leg with BROKKR_REQUIRE_BOUNDARY_EVIDENCE=1 and the controller's host run are where it runs.
   - I2: rename either_fence_refuses_unprotectable_writers_only_where_evidence_is_at_stake to what it now asserts, and correct the commit subject's "coordination stays keyed to evidence at stake", which is no longer true for boxed writers.
   - I3: a_forged_record_has_no_boxed_writer_to_forge_it's doc says "the lease kept". Assert the lease's bytes unchanged, or reword the doc to what the test asserts.
4. Re-run the gates and the suites of every crate the tree touches, on this base. Fix only what this base breaks. Run 3 saw capability_broker::cleanup::an_attempt_cancelled_during_initialization_or_a_call_settles_the_server_and_its_child fail once and then pass; if it fails again, capture its panic text in the evidence.
5. Update evidence/U9b1a.md: H3, the ruling, its tests and mutation, and the residuals that stay:
   - an unboxed writer can forge a record, but holds the user's write anyway (the later every-run decision ruling 21 names);
   - a writer admitted without a lease (any reach) is invisible to a later broker if a third party repairs the root's permissions while it lives; recorded as a follow-up, not fixed here.
   Write prose or a table, never a bullet list of gate lines.
6. Make ONE signed commit (`git commit -S`), with run 3's subject and body corrected per item 3 and a sentence on H3's fix. Report `complete`.

Do NOT start the enabling matrix, 42.2, SD4, the boxed end-to-end MCP proof, or L1/L2/L3 (TIOCSTI wiring binding, mutation records for the six tests, ruling 21's cases 1 and 4 through real dispatch). They are U9b1b's, and the controller carries them into U9b1b's brief. Do not report oversized or blocked for them.

Already ruled; do not ask again:
- Ruling 21's third case is proved by MB2's compile refusal.
- sources.rs keeps a brokering attempt's source lease.
- These stay LOW, recorded and not fixed: doctor's stale Linux text, opaque inline command seats refusing on Linux, and a named operator adapter qualifying only where another site opens adapters/.
- The wider no-lease residual in item 5 is recorded, not fixed (controller ruling on H3).
- settlement.rs:268 propagating lease failures only when staked fails safe (the lease stands). It is info, not yours.
- The verify checks artifact naming bundles/self is the controller's lane library, not yours.

Exact coverage and the crap ratchet are not yours. Record them as "not run in the seat".

This seat may hold Claude's own web-search and web-fetch tools. Use them only for published sources, and cite each URL you relied on in your notes.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U9b1a.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```
